messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE SUMMARY:

Admission Date: [insert date]
Discharge Date: [insert date]
Patient Name: [insert name]
Medical Record Number: [insert number]
Sex: Female 
Age: 21
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient presented to the Emergency Department (ED) complaining of right lower quadrant pain with associated nausea. The physical examination demonstrated tenderness in the lower right quadrant and guarding and rebound. The laboratory evaluation demonstrated leukocytosis, with a high white blood cell count and neutrophilia.
Imaging studies revealed the presence of an intrauterine gestational sac containing a fetal pole, with no adnexal lesions visible. A noncompressible fluid-filled, slightly hypervascular tubular structure was located in the right lower quadrant, measuring 16mm in diameter, confirming the diagnosis of acute appendicitis.
The patient was treated with intravenous antibiotics and underwent a laparoscopic appendectomy without any postoperative complications. The obstetric service examined the patient the next day, and the pregnancy remained intact. Repeat ultrasonography demonstrated a properly progressing pregnancy two weeks following the surgery.
The patient was discharged in stable condition and instructed to follow up with her obstetrician and the surgeon as necessary. Educational material regarding postoperative care and follow-up was provided.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Take medications as prescribed by your physician.
2. Continue follow-up appointments with your obstetrician and the surgeon as directed.
3. Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for four weeks.
4. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you experience fever, increasing pain, or wound drainage.
5. Use a stool softener as needed to prevent constipation.
6. Maintain a healthy diet and increase fluid intake.
7. Contact your healthcare provider if you have any questions or concerns.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**O99**

The patient has acute appendicitis in a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy. Under the ICD-10-AM pregnancy standard (ACS 1500), Chapter 15 codes take precedence for conditions arising during pregnancy. The exception is when the condition is documented as incidental to the pregnancy, which would use Z33. Nothing here says that. So the principal diagnosis falls in O99, specifically O99.6 for diseases of the digestive system complicating pregnancy. K35 (acute appendicitis) would be added as an additional code.
